headline: Dhaka seeks explanation after 2 Bangladeshis executed in Makkah
summary: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has summoned the Saudi Ambassador to demand details over the execution of two nationals on adultery charges.
details: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has sought an explanation from Saudi Ambassador Abdullah Zafer H bin Abiyah regarding the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in Makkah.
The two individuals were accused of engaging in adultery inside a mosque in Makkah, leading to their arrest, trial, and subsequent execution by Saudi authorities.
The Bangladesh government claims that neither the Ministry of Foreign Affairs nor the Bangladesh mission in Saudi Arabia were informed of the legal proceedings beforehand.
Dhaka only learned about the executions after they took place on October 14, prompting the government to seek detailed information.
A physical copy of a note verbale—a formal diplomatic communication—was handed over to the Saudi ambassador today to seek official clarification.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam confirmed the development, noting that Bilateral Affairs Secretary M Nazrul Islam met with the ambassador.
caption:
Two Bangladeshis were executed in Makkah on adultery charges without the Dhaka government being notified of the legal proceedings.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has sought an explanation from Saudi Ambassador Abdullah Zafer H bin Abiyah regarding the execution of two Bangladeshi nationals in Makkah.

The two individuals were accused of engaging in adultery inside a mosque in Makkah, leading to their arrest, trial, and subsequent execution by Saudi authorities.

The Bangladesh government claims that neither the Ministry of Foreign Affairs nor the Bangladesh mission in Saudi Arabia were informed of the legal proceedings beforehand.

Dhaka only learned about the executions after they took place on October 14, prompting the government to seek detailed information.

A physical copy of a note verbale—a formal diplomatic communication—was handed over to the Saudi ambassador today to seek official clarification.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam confirmed the development, noting that Bilateral Affairs Secretary M Nazrul Islam met with the ambassador.

#Bangladesh #SaudiArabia #Makkah #Diplomacy #ForeignAffairs

Source: The Daily Star, bdnews24.com, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo, Dhaka Tribune

headline: 2,088 hospitalised as 6 more die of dengue in 24 hours
summary: The DGHS reports a surge in admissions as the total death toll rises to 348 and cases reach 112,400.
details: At least six dengue patients died and 2,088 others were hospitalised in a 24-hour period, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The deaths occurred across several regions, with two reported in Dhaka North City Corporation, two in Dhaka South City Corporation, and one each in the Dhaka and Sylhet divisions.
With these latest figures, the total death toll from dengue has risen to 348, while the total number of cases has reached 112,400.
Currently, 6,026 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
caption:

With these latest figures, the total death toll from dengue has risen to 348, while the total number of cases has reached 112,400.

Currently, 6,026 dengue patients are undergoing treatment in hospitals across the country.
